context:
Treat this as copy driven by computed state. Fix the underlying summary
model first, then update rendered copy. Reuse RunIdentity for same-platform
labels and reuse the same comparable/missing query counts that feed the
normalized speedup chart.
description:
The 2026-05-09 post-completion review on develop dbac33ee1 found that Compare
summaries still make ambiguous or misleading claims. Same-platform comparisons
say "Polars is 1.00x faster" and "WINNER Polars" when both selected runs are
Polars v1.40.0 from different dates; Query Wins mixes comparable and missing
denominators; the empty Compare picker has duplicate SSB benchmark options;
and comparability copy says only benchmark and scale even though phase is also
required.

This item addresses review findings #8, #9, #10, and #13 recorded in
_project/audits/results-explorer-post-completion-review-2026-05-09.md. It
depends on compare-selection recovery so the Compare route is not edited in
two conflicting passes.

anti_patterns.dont: declare a winner when the displayed speedup is exactly 1.00x.
mix missing-query counts into comparable-query win denominators.
use platform name alone when multiple selected runs share it.

preserves.behavior: Comparable-only default behavior introduced by prior fixes remains intact.
Existing valid Compare deep links keep working.
Speedup charts still compute from the selected baseline.

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm test -- --run src/lib/__tests__/compareSummary.test.ts src/components/__tests__/CompareSummary.test.tsx src/components/__tests__/NormalizedSpeedupChart.test.tsx src/pages/__tests__/Compare.test.tsx
echo 'Manual/browser: same-platform compare names runs, handles 1.00x as tie/no material winner, and separates comparable vs missing counts'
verifications.description: Manual same-platform compare copy check passes
verifications.expected: manual evidence captured in PR notes or verification log

work_units.notes:
Prior art: PR #285 already labels the legacy slug
`"SSB (legacy slug)"` in
`results-explorer/src/lib/displayLabels.ts`, so the *labeling* half of
this work is shipped. Finding #10 reproduces if the Compare picker
builds its benchmark options from a source that yields both `ssb` and
`star_schema` as separate filter values.

Scope of this work unit is the filter-option list only: canonicalize
legacy aliases before rendering the Compare picker benchmark select so
exactly one SSB option appears, or — if both must remain visible for
data routing — keep the existing "SSB (legacy slug)" label and ensure
each option filters to a distinct, non-overlapping result set. If w0
cannot reproduce duplicate options against the current develop tip,
record the stale finding in the w0 log and skip implementation.
work_units.summary: Dedupe Compare benchmark filter options for the legacy SSB slug

work_units.notes:

by compact run identity, not just platform. If geomean speedup rounds to

work_units.summary: Use run identity and tie-aware language in same-platform summaries

work_units.notes:
Rewrite Query Wins and chart count copy so comparable-query counts and
excluded/missing-query counts are separate. Example target:
"4 fastest of 80 comparable; 69 queries excluded for missing data." Do
not add incomparable queries into the denominator used for win rates.

Update Compare guardrail text from "same benchmark and scale" to "same
benchmark, scale, and phase" wherever that is the actual winner-claim
requirement. Include primary metric where relevant if the code also
enforces it.
work_units.summary: Make comparability guardrail copy match the actual cohort lock
